J. | architecture = Renaissance | added = June 22, 1984 | area = {{convert|4.5|acre|sigfig=2}} | mpsub = {{NRHP url|id=64000496|title=Operating Passenger Railroad Stations TR}} | ref_num = 84002665{{NRISref|2009a}} }} | mapframe = yes | mapframe-custom = {{Infobox mapframe |shape=none |line=none |marker=rail |marker-color=#000 |zoom=14 }} }} '''Orange''' is an active [[commuter railroad]] [[train station]] in the [[City (New Jersey)|city]] of [[Orange, New Jersey|Orange]], [[Essex County, New Jersey|Essex County]], [[New Jersey]]. One of two stops in the city (along with [[Highland Avenue station (NJ Transit)|Highland Avenue]]), it is served by [[New Jersey Transit Rail Operations|New Jersey Transit]]'s [[Morris and Essex Lines]]: the [[Morristown Line]] to [[Hackettstown station|Hackettstown]] and the [[Gladstone Branch]] to [[Gladstone station (NJ Transit)|Gladstone]] for trains from [[Pennsylvania Station (New York City)|New York Penn Station]] and [[Hoboken Terminal]]. Orange station contains two low-level [[side platforms]] and three tracks. Orange station opened on November 19, 1836, with the opening of the [[Morris and Essex Railroad]] from [[Newark Broad Street Station|Newark]] to Orange. The station served as the western terminus of the line until September 28, 1837, when the railroad started operations west to [[Madison station (NJ Transit)|Madison station]].{{sfn|Walker|1902|p=409}} The current station depots and overhangs were built in 1918 with the elevation of tracks through the city by the [[Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad]]. The station depot at Orange station were added to the [[New Jersey Register of Historic Places|New Jersey]] and [[National Register of Historic Places|National Registers of Historic Places]] in 1984 as part of the [[Operating Passenger Railroad Stations Thematic Resource (New Jersey)|Operating Passenger Railroad Stations Thematic Resource]]. == History == The brick station and nearby freight terminal were built in 1918. The [[station building]] has been listed in the [[New Jersey Register of Historic Places|state]] and [[National Register of Historic Places|federal]] registers of historic places since 1984 and is part of the [[Operating Passenger Railroad Stations Thematic Resource (New Jersey)|Operating Passenger Railroad Stations Thematic Resource]].{{cite web | title=New Jersey and National Registers of Historic Places | url= http://www.nj.gov/dep/hpo/1identify/nrsr_lists.htm | publisher=[[New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection]] - Historic Preservation Office | access-date= 7 January 2015}}{{NRHP url|id=84002665|title=Orange New Jersey Transit Railroad Station Survey}} ==Station layout== Both platforms have walkways over their respective track allowing passengers to access Track 1, though trains on Track 1 do not typically stop at this station. == See also == * [[List of New Jersey Transit stations]] * [[National Register of Historic Places listings in Essex County, New Jersey]] ==Bibliography== *{{cite book |first=A.M.|last=Douglass|title=The Railroad Trainman, Volume 29 |date=1912 |publisher=Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen |location=[[Cleveland, Ohio]] |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AszNAAAAMAAJ |access-date=April 2, 2020}} *{{cite journal |last1=Walker |first1=Herbert T. |title=Early History of the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad and it's Locomotives -
